name: Cyclophosphamide Anhydrous

summary: A small computer model, rather than tests in people, estimated low risk scores for liver damage at 32 and heart damage at 40 [M]. The drug label includes warnings about bone marrow failure, weakened immune defenses that can cause severe or life-threatening infections, and a drop in blood cell counts called myelosuppression [3]. It also warns of harmful effects on the kidneys and urinary tract, such as bleeding in the bladder known as hemorrhagic cystitis, along with inflammation of the kidney and urinary tubes [3]. Regular monitoring of blood tests is required while using this medication [3].
